Every exclusion and inclusion the claim lists is in the question.

unruled:aqee#1.2.evidence: i8863 p. 4, Student qualifications 6 and 7. dependent.edu_line27 is computed only when dependent.edu_aoc; dependent.edu_aoc requires dependent.edu_student, which requires dependent.edu_student_tin -> dependent.edu_1098t ('Did the student receive a 2025 Form 1098-T ...', with the not-required exceptions and the request-and-cooperate procedure), and ends in dependent.edu_aoc_tin, which requires dependent.edu_ein ('Do you have the educational institution's employer identification number (EIN)'). person.edu_* likewise. A No to either leaves line 27 zero.

unruled:aqee#1.3.evidence: i8863 pp. 4, 9. The aqee definition computes both worksheet paths, but the callers choose one: dependent.edu_line27 to 30 take the AOC path only when dependent.edu_aoc, and dependent.edu_line31 takes ws4_llc only when dependent.edu_llc ('an eligible student who is not an American opportunity credit student'), else zero. One student never gets both.

unruled:asset#1.1.evidence: i4562 p. 10, 5-year property, "Appliances, carpets, furniture, etc., used in a rental real estate activity." (quote checked in sources/2025/i4562). An asset entry belongs to a Schedule C business (f4562 collection parent sc), and Schedule C refuses a rental activity: sc.passive asks whether 'the business is something other than a rental activity' and a No refuses through sc.screened. Rental real estate is Schedule E (rental), whose depreciation entries (rprop) ask the kind and refuse 'personal: something other than a building or part of one, such as an appliance, carpet, furniture' through rprop.personal (remedy 'Appliances, carpet, furniture, fences and other property that is not a building are outside this tool'). So rental-activity furniture never reaches asset.class. Residual not ruled a gap: furniture of a non-rental lodging business on Schedule C (stays of 7 days or less with services) is not a 'rental real estate activity' under the quoted line.

unruled:asset#1.2.evidence: p946 p. 35, Depreciation Methods for Farm Property, "If you place personal property in service in a farming business after 1988, and before 2018, you must generally depreciate it under GDS using the 150% declining balance method"; i4562 p. 12 (quotes checked in sources/2025/p946 and i4562). Farm income is refused for 2025 by scope.farm ('In 2025, did you ... have income or a loss from farming?'), and asset entries belong to a Schedule C business, which is not a farming business (farming is Schedule F); agricultural classes 01.x map to outside in class_lives (asset.outside), and the 263A(d)(3) and electing-farming ADS cases are in asset.ads_required. 15- and 20-year property already takes the 150% DB tables. Residual not ruled a gap: an asset placed in service before 2018 in a farm the filer no longer runs and later moved into the Schedule C business, a rare case no screen names.

unruled:f1040#1.1.evidence: i1040gi p. 13, 'Generally, a married couple can't file a joint return if either spouse is a nonresident alien at any time during the year'; i1040gi p. 14, 'To make either choice for 2025, you and your spouse must file a joint return and attach a statement'; p501 p. 6, divorce to remarry. (1) A joint return with a spouse who was a nonresident alien for any part of 2025: scope.nonresident ('For any part of 2025, were you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) a nonresident alien, that is, neither a U.S. citizen nor a U.S. resident for tax?', help 'A Yes ends the interview here', asked after scope.noncitizen) refuses through scope.other_income; executed on a copy of scope.ch11.wage_only_debtor (chapter 11 No) with scope.noncitizen and scope.nonresident true: f1040.line12e, line 24 and scope.ready are refusals at scope.other_income. (3) The residual: a spouse treated as a resident under a section 6013(g) choice can truthfully answer No to scope.nonresident (its help speaks only of a green card), and the tool then prepares the joint return with no prompt for the statement the choice requires in its first year. Same cause and same proposed fix (say in scope.nonresident's help that a 6013(g) spouse answers Yes) as BUG-0828 (the NIIT side of the 6013(g) joint return); cited, not filed again. Low.

unruled:f2441#1.1.evidence: i2441 p. 2; p503 pp. 3, 8, 10, quoted. Column (d) is not a raw total: it is dependent.dc_paid, asked per qualifying person, and its interview prompt states each rule the claim lists: care 'for the time this person was under 13 or not able to care for themselves' (status day by day; a child turning 13 is also asked dependent.dc_under13 and dependent.dc_over12_care); 'your share of the employment taxes'; the housekeeper's meals; leave out 'school from kindergarten up, summer school, tutoring and overnight camp', 'food, lodging, clothing, schooling and entertainment, unless food or schooling comes with the care and cannot be separated', 'amounts a state social services agency paid back to you, and expenses you claim as medical expenses', 'child support', 'a chauffeur, bartender or gardener', care outside the home for anyone but a dependent child under 13 who does not spend 8 hours a day in the home, 'a care center that does not meet all state and local rules'; days of work only, and 'If a cost was only partly for work, count that part'. f2441.other_care_expenses (line 16 inputs) asks only for 2025 care not in the per-person amounts, i.e. care of the same kind. The reviewer saw the f2441 lines, not the dependent entry's question.

unruled:f2441#1.2.evidence: i2441 p. 1, Qualifying Person(s), 'Your disabled spouse who wasn't physically or mentally able to care for themselves and lived with you for more than half the year'. The tool never counts a spouse as a qualifying person: f2441.unable ('In 2025, was there a time when you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) could not care for yourself ...', help 'Answer Yes too if some of the care you paid for was for your husband or wife. A Yes ends the interview here.') feeds f2441.student_disabled, which refuses on lines 4, 5, 18 and 19 ('... and a disabled spouse as a qualifying person, are outside this tool'). On a separate return the help still names care for the husband or wife. Other qualifying persons are dependents tested by dependent.dc_lived_half (dependent.dc_disabled_qp), so the half-year test is applied where the tool computes.

unruled:f4562#1.1.evidence: i4562 p. 5, Lines 5 to 12. f4562.line12 copies sc.s179_allowed, the business's share of the return's Part I (s179): s179.line5 with the married-filing-separately 50% share (s179.line5_mfs) and a refusal of any section 179 election or carryover on a separate return (s179.mfs, so the different-allocation election never arises); line 6 sums person.s179_nonlisted (listed property is on line 7); trade-ins are refused by asset.got_other ('Did you get it with a trade-in...') and scveh.got_other; line 10 is the 2024 line 13 carryover (s179.prior_form, s179.carryover); line 11 is s179.income0 from the Schedule C profits figured without section 179 (person.income179) plus Form 1040 line 1a wages, combined for both spouses, with working-capital interest (s179.wc_interest); asset.s179 limits the election to property used in the active conduct of the business. unruled:f4562#1.10.evidence: i4562 p. 13, Part V, Form 2106 and Schedule C Part IV (quotes checked). Where the vehicle information is reported changes no amount. unruled:f4562#1.2.evidence: i4562 p. 9, Line 17, partial dispositions and "Prior years' depreciation, plus current year's depreciation, can never exceed the depreciable basis" (checked). A disposal of part of the asset in 2025 is refused by asset.ended_this_year ('did you sell, give away or scrap it or part of it'); a portion disposed of in an earlier year changed its basis other than by depreciation, refused by asset.basis_changed; both are in asset.screen and refuse through asset.screened. The cap holds by construction: asset.macrs_prior applies the MACRS percentage table rates (which sum to 100%) to the unadjusted basis after section 179 and the allowance (asset.ub_prior), and is zero after the last recovery year (asset.done).

unruled:f4562#1.3.evidence: i4562 pp. 9, 11-12 (quotes checked). What is encoded: the business-use basis (asset.basis from asset.cost x asset.pct), section 179 and the allowance before MACRS (asset.after179, asset.ub), and the mid-quarter 40% test (form mq, mq.applies, with asset.quarter/asset.qconv). What is refused through asset.screen (asset.screened): basis reductions by credits or deductions other than section 179 and the allowance (asset.basis_changed), the straight line and 150% DB elections (asset.method_other), property disposed of in 2025 (asset.ended_this_year), and property acquired in a like-kind exchange or involuntary conversion (asset.got_other). Converted property is placed in service on the conversion date (asset.placed help).

unruled:f4562#1.4.evidence: i4562 p. 11 (quotes checked). Trees and vines bearing fruits or nuts are farm property: their class is outside in class_lives (asset.outside, 'Certain Property for Which Recovery Periods Assigned' and agricultural classes) and farm income is refused by scope.farm. unruled:f4562#1.5.evidence: i4562 pp. 11-13, ADS and real property (quotes checked). asset.kind_excluded refuses buildings and their parts and land ('Is this a building or part of one, land, ...'); asset.ads_required refuses property that must use ADS and asset.method_other an ADS election; asset.outside_use refuses property used outside the US and tax-exempt use property; all refuse through asset.screened, so lines 19g to 19j and 20a to 20e are never reached for a Schedule C asset. unruled:f4562#1.6.evidence: i4562 pp. 13-14, Line 25 (quotes checked). unruled:f8606#1.1.evidence: i8606 pp. 2, 9. Line 1 is person.ira_nondeductible, figured from IRA Deduction Worksheet lines 10 to 12 on person.ira_trad, whose question leaves out SEP or SIMPLE contributions and contributions taken back with their earnings by the deadline (help: 'Leave out rollovers, repayments of a reservist distribution, ... anything you took back out with its earnings by the deadline for your return, ... and SEP or SIMPLE contributions'). Recharacterization is refused by person.ira_excess (person.ira_recharacterized); contributions above the limit by person.ira_over_limit and person.ira_extra_left. A repayment of a qualified reservist distribution (to be added to line 1) is refused for the whole return: scope.reservist_repaid ('did you ... put back into an IRA money taken out of a retirement plan during a call to active duty as a reservist?') is in scope.other_income, which refuses Form 1040. unruled:f8606#1.2.evidence: i8606 p. 2. A Roth IRA distribution other than a qualified one (code Q), inherited or not, is refused by retirement.bad_code. A traditional IRA distribution with basis is refused through retirement.special (retirement.ira_basis_if_trad) and f8606.dist; the beneficiary of an inherited IRA with the decedent's basis may answer that question No, which is the open BUG-0871 (see retirement#1.2). The stand-alone Form 8606 for a person not required to file a return is outside a tool that prepares a Form 1040 (no return is filed); presentation only.

unruled:household#1.1.evidence: p501 p. 9, "If you pay more than half the cost of keeping your parent in a rest home or home for the elderly, that counts as paying more than half the cost of keeping up your parent's main home" and "for the entire part of the year your parent was alive". unruled:household#1.2.evidence: p501 pp. 9-10; i1040gi p. 44. unruled:household#1.3.evidence: i1040gi p. 14, "If the child isn't claimed as your dependent, enter the child's name in the entry space below qualifying surviving spouse"; p501 p. 8. unruled:sales#1.1.evidence: p550 pp. 80-81. sd.small_business_stock ('did you ... lose money on stock that a small company issued to you, a loss you claim as an ordinary loss and not a capital loss (section 1244 or section 1242 stock)?'), asked of every filer, is part of sd.other_forms and refuses ('The ordinary loss is claimed on Form 4797'). unruled:sc#1.1.evidence: p587 p. 3; i1040sc p. 13. A profit-seeking activity that is not a business is refused by sc.special ('it is a hobby, or an occasional activity not run for profit', sc.screened). The storage use is asked only for 'its stock or samples' with the home as 'its only fixed place of business' (sc.ho_uses), which is the retail or wholesale case. That the space is 'separately identifiable' is not asked; accepted as a low-residual detail.

unruled:sc#1.2.evidence: i1040sc p. 9, Line 23, 'Do not deduct ... Estate and gift taxes. Taxes assessed to pay for improvements, such as paving and sewers.' The interview help of sc.line23 says 'Leave out ... charges for improvements such as paving or sewers' (the claim read only the form-YAML source). The prompt asks what 'this business pay[s] ... in business taxes and licenses' with business examples. unruled:sc#1.3.evidence: i1040sc p. 6, Medicaid waiver payments (Notice 2014-7). So the Schedule C line 1 plus Part V offset never arises.

unruled:scope#1.1.evidence: i1040gi pp. 23-24, 91, 100. unruled:scveh#1.1.evidence: i1040sc p. 8, Line 20a, 'if you leased a vehicle for a term of 30 days or more, you may have to reduce your deduction by the inclusion amount'; p946 p. 59; p463 (2025), Inclusion Amounts, the amount applies if the vehicle's FMV when the lease began was more than $62,000 (2025 leases). But the interview names the case only by its official term with no plain description (N6), so a filer leasing an expensive car, truck or van who does not know the term answers No and keeps the full lease deduction on line 20a. Filed as a low wording defect of the gate (BUG-0780).

unruled:s179#1.1.evidence: p946 pp. 17-18; i4562 p. 5. Checked per property: a trade-in, like-kind exchange, involuntary conversion or purchase from a related person is asset.got_other ('Did you get it with a trade-in, in an exchange, ... from a relative or a business you control'), and use predominantly outside the United States is asset.outside_use; both make asset.screened true, which refuses the property. Land is real property, refused by asset.screened; land improvements, investment property, property bought and leased to others (with the noncorporate-lessor exceptions in the help) and use by exempt, governmental or foreign users are asset.not179, and an election on such property is refused by asset.s179_bad ('or it is not section 179 property'). The $31,300 heavy SUV cap is applied to vehicles (a scveh entry) by scveh.suv_cap and scveh.s179_bad. So no disqualified or traded-in cost reaches line 6.

unruled:s179#1.2.evidence: p946 pp. 18-19, Joint return after filing separate returns: 'If you and your spouse elect to amend your separate returns by filing a joint return after the due date'. That joint return replaces separate returns already filed, an amended return (Form 1040-X); the tool prepares the original 2025 return and asks nothing about earlier filings. A separate return with a section 179 election or carryover is itself refused (s179.mfs at s179.line5), so no separate return made by this tool carries an election. No gate names the amended case; residual accepted as before (earlier s179#1.4).

unruled:s179#1.3.evidence: i4562 p. 5; p946 p. 19, active conduct means meaningful participation. s179.income_sc sums person.income179, i.e. Schedule C line 31 before section 179 only. Every Schedule C is asked sc.passive (line G: 'did you yourself do all or most of the work of this business, or work in it more than 500 hours?', with the other material-participation tests in the help); a No makes sc.screened true and refuses the business. Material participation is a stricter test than meaningful participation, so every business counted is actively conducted. The one Yes not based on work, an oil or gas working interest, deducts depletion, which sc.special refuses (same gate). Other trades or businesses (partnerships, rentals, farms) are refused by scope.schedule1.

unruled:s179#1.4.evidence: p946 p. 19, the eight steps 'if you have a taxable income limit for some other deduction'. The steps are needed only when each limit depends on the other. i4562 p. 5, Line 11: business income is 'computed without regard to any section 179 expense deduction, the deduction for one-half of self-employment taxes ... or any net operating loss deduction'. It does not subtract self-employed retirement contributions (Schedule 1), so the SEP or SIMPLE limit (person.plan) is figured after line 12 in one pass, which is what the encoding does. The interdependent case this tool can reach, the home office simplified-method gross income limit together with the section 179 business income limit, is refused by sc.ho_both_limits at sc.ho_both ('Figuring two income-based limits in the order of Pub. 946 is outside this tool').

unruled:f8889#1.1.evidence: i8889 p. 8; i5329 p. 8. unruled:f8889#1.3.evidence: p969 pp. 8-9; i8889 p. 8. f8889.medical lists 'long-term care insurance' premiums with no age-based limit (p502 lists $480 to $6,020 for 2025), and says costs must date from after you opened the HSA without the rule that an HSA funded by a rollover is established when the prior account was. unruled:f8889#1.5.evidence: i8889 p. 4, Line 1. The self-only/family checkbox is not encoded, but the amounts it would select are figured from the coverage answers: f8889.coverage_year (self-only all year, family all year, or changed, counted month by month) and f8889.dec_coverage for the last-month rule set line 3. unruled:f7203#1.1.evidence: i7203 p. 1, Who Must File, quoted. Both triggers are refused on the K-1 itself, not behind f7203.required: k1s.basis_carry is asked on every K-1 (no gate; 'Was a loss or deduction from this corporation held back on an earlier return because your basis in it was too low?') and refuses at k1s.ok (Form 7203 Part III column (b)); a loan repayment is box 16 code E, refused through k1s.box16ef_if_16 ('code E (repayment of loans from you)'). Every K-1 also refuses at scope.k1 until the integration lane wires the totals.

unruled:f7203#1.2.evidence: i7203 p. 4, Column (b), quoted. Column (b) is refused, not dropped: k1s.basis_carry (asked on every K-1) refuses with 'Form 7203, Part III, column (b), and Schedule E (Form 1040), line 27'; f7203's note says so.

unruled:f7203#1.3.evidence: i7203 p. 4, column (a), quoted. Lines 39 to 46 take boxes 11 and 12 (section 179, charitable contributions, investment interest, 59(e)(2), other deductions), box 16 code F (foreign taxes) and box 17 code R (oil and gas depletion); each is refused on the K-1: k1s.box11_12, k1s.box16ef_if_16, k1s.box17_other_if_17. unruled:f7203#1.4.evidence: i7203 p. 2, Line 2: section 351 'carryover basis of assets transferred ... less the liabilities assumed', section 357(c); 'The basis for stock received as compensation is the FMV on the date the compensation is included in income'. Partly covered: f7203.line2 help gives inherited (value at death) and gifted (giver's basis) shares, and f7203.line1 help covers a first year ('If you first got shares in 2025, enter 0 and give what they cost'). Not covered: property contributed (adjusted basis less liabilities; 357(c)) and stock received for services. Low.

unruled:f7203#1.5.evidence: i7203 p. 2, 'aren't part of a shareholder's loan basis except to the extent the shareholder makes a payment on the loan guaranteed or co-signed'. f7203.loans help says 'Loans you guaranteed or co-signed for the corporation are not meant' with no exception for payments made, so such a shareholder answers No, Part II is not refused, and losses are limited by stock basis alone (understated deduction). Low.

unruled:f7203#1.6.evidence: i7203 p. 2, Name of Shareholder and Item D, quoted. The per-spouse split is already encoded: f7203 is an implicit entry under each k1s entry (collection parent k1s), and each K-1 is issued to one shareholder, so spouses with their own K-1s get their own Form 7203. Item D (how the stock was acquired) is a checkbox with no amount.

unruled:f8582#1.1.evidence: i8582 p. 1, Exception, 'If you're married filing separately, you lived apart from your spouse all year'. The $12,500 and $50,000 limits are applied (f8582.exception uses params f8582.exception_loss and f8582.exception_magi, mfs values 1,250,000 and 5,000,000 cents), but living apart is not tested. Rechecked on this tree: x1sche.f2.small_loss_exception with f1040.status mfs, household.married_dec31 true and household.mfs_living together_late gives f8582.exception true, line 9 $213.20 and s1.line5 -$213.20, identical to mfs_living apart_all_year; no refusal. Recorded in BUG-0836 (unfixed). The rest is refused: passive credits (prior-year Form 8582-CR at s3.prior_forms_if_forms; K-1 credits at k1p.r_b15 and k1s.box13_other), limited-partner and estate or trust interests (every K-1 at scope.k1 through scope.schedule1).

unruled:f8582#1.2.evidence: i8582 p. 10, 'Married individuals who file separate returns and lived with their spouses at any time during the tax year don't qualify under the active participation rule and must use Part V'; p. 4, 'The special allowance isn't available ...'. rental.part4 is rental.active alone, and f8582.line5 to line9 ignore household.mfs_living: witness as f8582#1.1 (together_late: line 8 $12,500, line 9 $213.20). BUG-0836 (unfixed) proposes f8582.mfs_together zeroing line 9 and the exception, which has the Part V effect. The other two tests are refused: less than 10%, rental.under_tenth ('A rental you own less than 10% of is outside this tool'); limited partner, every K-1 at scope.k1.

unruled:f8582#1.3.evidence: i8582 pp. 2-4, quoted. Each case is refused on this tree: real estate professional, sche.re_pro (refuses at sche.line26, 'A real estate professional's rentals are outside this tool'); section 280A(c)(5) home use, rental.ws51 (Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1); average stay 7 days or less, rental.stay7_if_short; significant or extraordinary services (and so the 30-days-with-services case), rental.services ('reported on Schedule C; this tool does not prepare it'). A trade or business with material participation is not a Schedule E rental entry. Rental incidental to a nonrental activity is rare for Schedule E Part I property and not filed. Not every Schedule E rental is treated as passive: the refusals remove the listed cases first.

unruled:f8582#1.4.evidence: i8582 p. 11, Line 6, quoted. f8582.magi_adj adds s1 lines 11, 13, 16-19a and 25, and s1.line25 is line 24a only (jury duty; 'lines 24b to 24z are outside this tool and refused ... by scope.schedule1'), so no 501(c)(18) deduction can be in it; a W-2 box 12 code H is refused by scope.w2_marks_if_w2 through scope.schedule1. unruled:f8582#1.5.evidence: i8582 p. 11, Line 9 and the CRD worksheet, quoted; p. 1, Reminders, 'If you have prior-year unallowed CRDs limited by the passive loss rules, you may continue to include them'. The CRD survives only as a prior-year unallowed amount from a pre-2010 building; f8582.line3 records that it is not asked. Not asked and not refused: an extremely rare carryforward, not filed (as the earlier ruling of this unit). The part2 gate requiring a loss on line 1d is the no-CRD rule of Form 8582 line 3.

unruled:k1p#1.1.evidence: i1040se pp. 9-10 and i1065sk1 pp. 11, 13, quoted. No k1p question or refusal covers unreimbursed partnership expenses, interest on debt to buy the interest, or losses carried from earlier years by the basis or at-risk limits (k1s has k1s.basis_carry and k1s.risk_carry; k1p has neither; k1p.basis_short asks only about 2025 losses): BUG-0841. unruled:k1p#1.2.evidence: i1065sk1 p. 22, Code A, 'reduce this amount ... by any section 179 expense deduction claimed, unreimbursed partnership expenses claimed, and depletion'. unruled:k1p#1.3.evidence: i1040se p. 9, fuel credit claimed on the 2024 return 'enter as income in column (h) or column (k)'. Nothing asks about it (k1p.r_b15 and k1p.r_b20 screen only the 2025 K-1). Low; latent (scope.k1).

unruled:k1p#1.4.evidence: i1065sk1 p. 8, 'Working interests in oil or gas wells if you were a general partner'; p. 11, recharacterized income. k1p.b1_passive is k1p.material false; no question asks about a working interest, and a general partner with more than 100 hours who answers No to k1p.t4 has significant participation income left passive. Farmers' special rules: farming is refused at scope.farm. Latent (scope.k1).

unruled:k1p#1.5.evidence: i1065sk1 p. 9, work as an investor not counted, quoted. k1p.work's help: 'Count work in running the business. Reading its reports or checking on it as an investor does not count'; k1p.hours500 counts 'that work'. The anti-abuse prong (work not usually done by owners, done mainly to avoid the limits) is not stated; it turns on the filer's purpose and is not filed.

unruled:k1p#1.6.evidence: i1065sk1 p. 14, box 2 'isn't from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated'. sche.re_pro is read only by sche.line26. Personal use of a partnership dwelling is not asked. Latent (scope.k1).

unruled:k1p#1.7.evidence: i1065sk1 p. 30, 'only those items that are qualified items ... included or allowed in determining taxable income for the tax year'. k1p.box20z_if_any is the statement's QBI; the scaling by the allowed share of a held-back box 1 loss (k1p.qbi, D-K7) is listed for the integration lane in the k1p wiring contract and not encoded. Latent (scope.k1).

unruled:k1p#1.8.evidence: i1065sk1 p. 13, fiscal year 'report the amounts on your tax return for the year in which the partnership's fiscal year ends'; p. 9, 'participation during the partnership's tax year'. No question asks the partnership's tax year; k1p.work, k1p.hours500, k1p.most_hours, k1p.nearly_all, k1p.t4 and k1p.t7 ask about calendar 2025. Low; latent (scope.k1).

unruled:k1s#1.1.evidence: i1120ssk p. 6 and p. 4, quoted (checked in sources). k1s.p2_loss/p2_income are passive whatever the facts; no k1s question or refusal names a real estate professional, and sche.re_pro is read only by sche.line26 (Schedule E Part I), so it does not reach K-1 box 2. unruled:k1s#1.3.evidence: i8582 p. 10, Part IV column (c), quoted. k1s.p4_prior_raw = k1s.b2_prior_if_any when k1s.part4 (this year's active participation and 10% only); k1s has no counterpart of rental.prior_not_active, so a held-back box 2 loss from a year without active participation goes in Part IV. Every K-1 still refuses at scope.k1 (scope.schedule1), so this is latent until the integration lane wires the person.k1s_* totals.

unruled:k1s#1.4.evidence: i1120ssk p. 5, quoted. k1s.p2_* and k1s.p3_* are passive always; no tick or refusal for a dwelling used personally by a shareholder (14 days / 10%) or a trading activity. Every K-1 still refuses at scope.k1 (scope.schedule1), so this is latent until the integration lane wires the person.k1s_* totals.

unruled:k1s#1.5.evidence: i1120ssk p. 4, quoted. The help of k1s.work says 'Work as the corporation's employee counts. Work done only as an investor, such as reading its reports, does not.' The anti-abuse prong (work not usually done by owners, done mainly to avoid the passive rules) turns on intent and is not filed, as ruled for k1p#1.5.

unruled:k1s#1.6.evidence: i1120ssk p. 6 and p. 4, quoted. No k1s question asks the corporation's tax year; k1s.work, hours500, most_hours and mp_other ask about calendar 2025. unruled:k1s#1.7.evidence: i1120ssk p. 6 and p. 9, quoted. s1.ebl_total = s1.ebl_sc + s1.ebl_sche (Schedules C and Schedule E Part I); k1s.col_i and the allowed passive box 1 loss enter no excess business loss total, and no k1s refusal covers it. unruled:royalty#1.3.evidence: i1040se p. 6 (quoted, checked). royalty.line4 takes every royalty as ordinary Schedule E income; nothing asks or refuses a patent-transfer royalty or a coal or iron ore disposal that may be the sale of a capital asset. unruled:royalty#1.4.evidence: i1040se p. 6, Line 10 (quoted, checked). royalty.amt10 asks 'Legal and other professional fees for it, paid in 2025; zero if none' with no help and no exclusion of title-defense, recovery or development fees; the amount is line 10. Same as BUG-0922 (open, low).

unruled:royalty#1.5.evidence: i1040se p. 6 and p. 7 (quoted, checked). royalty.amt19 asks 'Other costs of it (not depletion), paid in 2025; zero if none': own labor is excluded by 'paid', but capital investments and improvements are not; BUG-0922 (open, low). unruled:royalty#1.6.evidence: i1040se p. 4, Line A (quoted, checked): a Yes/No checkbox about the filer's own duty to file Forms 1099; it changes no amount. No Schedule E line A is encoded for rentals or royalties (as the xrel ruling).

unruled:rprop#1.1.evidence: i4562 p. 11 and i1040se p. 6, quoted. A rental of part of a property the filer lives in is refused at rental.part_home ('Is it part of a property you also live in, such as a room in your home or one unit of a building you live in?', refusal on rental.line21); for any other rental the whole building is rented and personal-use days divide line 18 (rental.div18). unruled:rprop#1.2.evidence: i4562 p. 9, quoted. rprop.screen names no like-kind exchange or involuntary conversion; a 2025 exchange of real estate is refused at sd.like_kind, but a building received in an earlier exchange is depreciated by rprop.rate from its own placed-in-service date. unruled:sche#1.1.evidence: i1040se p. 5, quoted. unruled:sche#1.2.evidence: i1040se p. 5, quoted. unruled:sche#1.3.evidence: i1040se p. 3-4 and i8582 p. 11, quoted. unruled:rental#1.1.evidence: Two cases. (2) Married filing separately and lived with the spouse (i8582 p. 4, 'The special allowance isn't available if you were married, are filing a separate return for the year, and lived with your spouse at any time during the year'; p. 10, 'must use Part V instead of Part IV'): separate returns are now supported and nothing refuses or zeroes this. rental.part4 is rental.active alone; f8582 reads no household.mfs_living helper. unruled:rental#1.10.evidence: i1040se p. 3, At-Risk Rules (quoted, checked). rental.not_at_risk asks only 'Is any of the money you put into it borrowed on a loan you are not personally liable for, other than a loan from a bank or other lender in the business of lending (for example, a loan from the seller)?' (refusal at rental.line22). unruled:rental#1.2.evidence: i8582 p. 3 to 4, Exceptions (quoted, checked): extraordinary personal services, rental incidental to holding for investment (under 2% of the smaller of unadjusted basis or FMV), defined-business-hours nonexclusive use, and property provided to a partnership, S corporation or joint venture in the owner's capacity. The encoding screens average stays (rental.short_stays, rental.stay7, refused at rental.line21_full), significant services (rental.services, 'such as cleaning during their stay, changing linen or meals', refused) and self-rental (rental.kind self_rental, 'property rented to a business you or your spouse run', refused), which reach extraordinary services and property used by the filer's own business only in part. unruled:rental#1.3.evidence: i1040se p. 6 (quoted, checked). Same as BUG-0779 (open, low), whose symptom and proposed tick name dealer property. A Yes ends the interview here.') feeds the scope.schedule1 refusal.

unruled:rental#1.4.evidence: i1040se p. 5, Line 3 (quoted, checked): FMV of services or property received as rent goes on line 3. rental.rents asks 'Rent received for it in 2025 (your share), including advance rent and expenses a tenant paid for you', help 'Include a security deposit you kept and repairs a tenant paid for in place of rent'; the amount is line 3. A filer who received property or services in place of rent counts it as rent received and it reaches the line. Residual: services other than repairs are not named in the help; a wording low, not filed (as the xrel ruling).

unruled:rental#1.5.evidence: p527 pp. 26 to 27 (quoted, checked). Four parts. (1) Family member using it as a main home at a fair rent: covered, rental.personal_any help 'Not personal use: family renting at a fair rent as their main home'. (2) Main-home days left out of the single personal-day count that also drives the expense division ('this special rule doesn't apply when dividing expenses'): rental.days_personal tells the filer to leave them out and the same answer feeds rental.total_c and every rental.div* line; BUG-0775 (open, medium; witness in the entry: a June 1 conversion deducts the full year's lines 9, 12 and 16). (3) A shorter rental ended by a sale or exchange: BUG-0772 (open, low). (4) A co-owner renting it as a main home under a shared equity financing agreement: rental.personal_any counts 'another owner' and its help does not exclude this case; filed as BUG-0926 (low). The ruling cites the medium entry.

unruled:rental#1.6.evidence: i1040se p. 7, Lines 12 and 13 (quoted, checked). Prepaid interest and points: rental.amt12 ('Mortgage interest on it shown on Form 1098 (box 1), your share, paid in 2025') and rental.amt13 ('Other interest on loans for it (no Form 1098 in your name), paid in 2025') exclude neither, and nothing spreads points over the loan; points entered as other interest are deducted at once. Filed as BUG-0925 (low). Not gaps: Form 8990 (i8990, Exclusions from filing, archived and checked: a small business taxpayer with average gross receipts of $31 million or less is not required to file; a rental treated as a QBI business is refused at sche.qbi_business); a Form 1098 issued to a co-borrower is line 13, which rental.amt13 asks ('no Form 1098 in your name'). Interest beyond the Form 1098 amount on the same loan has no stated place: named in the same entry. Use-of-proceeds allocation stays BUG-0777.

unruled:rental#1.7.evidence: i1040se p. 6, Line 10 (quoted, checked). rental.amt10 asks 'Legal fees and other professional fees, such as tax preparation for the rental, paid in 2025' with no help and no exclusion of title-defense, recovery or development fees; the amount goes to line 10. Same as BUG-0776 (open, low).

unruled:rental#1.8.evidence: i1040se p. 7, Line 17 (quoted, checked): the base rate of the first telephone line into the filer's residence is personal. A rental that is part of a property the filer lives in is refused (rental.part_home, 'Is it part of a property you also live in, such as a room in your home or one unit of a building you live in?', refuses at rental.line21_full). For any other rental, rental.amt17 asks 'Utilities you paid' under the heading 'Did you pay any of these for it in 2025?', the rental's utilities; the filer's own home phone line is not one. No amount a filer would enter is wrong (as the xrel ruling).

unruled:rental#1.9.evidence: i1040se p. 6 (quoted, checked). Own labor: not a gap, every cost question asks an amount 'paid in 2025'. Capital investments: rental.amt19 'Other costs of renting it (not depreciation), paid in 2025' and rental.amt7 'Cleaning and maintenance (not repairs), paid in 2025' do not exclude capital purchases or improvements (only rental.amt14's help names improvements); BUG-0776 (open, low). Form 8826 credit and deduction for the same cost: not a gap here. The tool computes no Form 8826 credit (no rental question asks for it; Form 3800 credits are refused only for a Schedule C), so a return it prepares cannot take both.

unruled:rf4562#1.1.evidence: i1040se p. 7, Line 18: Form 4562 is needed for listed property, a section 179 deduction or amortization beginning in 2025. Each case is refused before rf4562.needed matters: a vehicle at rental.vehicle ('Car, truck or travel costs for it', refuses at rental.line21_full); any other listed property is personal property, refused at rprop.personal; a section 179 deduction or special allowance at rprop.screen ('you deducted any of its cost in one year (a special allowance or section 179) or depreciate it another way'). Amortization: no rental cost the encoding takes is amortized on Form 4562 (points on a rental loan are interest under p527, OID rules, not Form 4562 amortization); a startup-type amortization does not arise in a Schedule E Part I rental of the kinds kept. Effect presentation only (whether the form is attached).

unruled:rf4562#1.2.evidence: i1040se p. 7; i4562 p. 9, Line 17. rprop.screen refuses 'you sold, gave away or stopped renting it in 2025' (use ended, partial disposition) and 'its basis changed after you began depreciating it, other than by depreciation', and ADS or other methods. Prior depreciation cannot exceed basis under the tables used: eval of x1sche.f2.small_loss_exception with the building placed in service February 1997, 1996, 1990 and before 1987 gives rprop.recovery_year 29, 30, 36, 40 and rprop.rate 0, rprop.dep $0 (the recovery period has ended), so line 17 takes nothing beyond the basis.

unruled:rf4562#1.3.evidence: i1040se p. 7; i4562 p. 9. Land: rprop.basis asks 'what you paid for the building or improvement, not the land', with help 'the price (with closing costs) less the part for the land; your property tax bill's split of land and building may be used' (covered). Placed in service: rprop.month/rprop.year ask when 'it was first ready and available for rent (placed in service)' (covered). Like-kind exchange or involuntary conversion in 2025 (the carryover-basis rule and its election): trading real estate or rental property is sd.sold_other and sd.business_property, and a condemnation or casualty is on sd.other_forms; eval of the rental fixture with sd.sold_other and sd.business_property true refuses f1040.line11a at sd.other_forms (Form 8824/4797/4684 outside the tool). An exchange of an earlier year is depreciated from the filer's existing schedule ($rprop help 'Your earlier depreciation schedule lists them').

unruled:rf4562#1.4.evidence: Same as rf4562#1.3, for line 19j (nonresidential real property placed in service in 2025): land excluded by rprop.basis and its help; placed-in-service date asked as first ready and available for rent (rprop.month/rprop.year); a 2025 like-kind exchange or involuntary conversion is refused at sd.other_forms (eval: sd.sold_other and sd.business_property true refuse f1040.line11a at sd.other_forms).

unruled:sc#1.4.evidence: i1040sc p. 5, Line 1: 'If the total amounts that were reported in box 1 of Forms 1099-NEC are more than the total you are reporting on line 1, attach a statement explaining the difference.' The statement is filing information and changes no amount. As the earlier ruling on this sentence (sc#1.3 under the previous subject).

unruled:f5695#1.11.evidence: i5695 pp. 6-7. As the earlier rulings of these claims, rechecked against the current lines.

unruled:dependent#1.2.evidence: i8863 p. 6, Tip: "If you paid qualified education expenses in both 2025 and 2026 for an academic period that begins in the first 3 months of 2026 and you receive tax-free educational assistance or a refund, as described above, you may choose to reduce the qualified education expenses you paid in 2026 instead of reducing the qualified education expenses you paid in 2025." Checked: dependent.edu_a_this_year, edu_a_next_year and edu_refunds ask only the amounts, and dependent.edu_adj_sum subtracts them from the 2025 expenses always; no question asks for the choice, no refusal covers it, and no earlier ruling or ambiguity entry names it. The tool computes the default treatment, so the 2025 credit can be lower than the filer may claim; recorded as BUG-0932 (low).

unruled:household#1.4.evidence: i1040gi p. 15, Qualifying Surviving Spouse, "If the child isn't claimed as your dependent, enter the child's name in the entry space." As household#1.3: the status is figured (household.qss_eligible) and the entry space is a printed-form entry with no notice line; no amount changes.

unruled:mq#1.3.evidence: p946 p. 34. Nonresidential real property, residential rental property and railroad grading or tunnel bores never reach mq.applies: Schedule C real property is refused by asset.screen ('it is real property ... or land'); rental buildings are rprop entries depreciated with the mid-month tables (rprop.rate, Table A-6/A-7a) and are not in mq.q4 or mq.total, which sum Schedule C assets and vehicles only.

unruled:rec#1.1.evidence: i1040gi p. 92, Line 8z, 'List the type and amount of income. If necessary, include a statement'. The description and statement are filing information; rec.to_line8z gives the amount, which is what line 8z adds.

unruled:refund#1.2.evidence: p525 pp. 24-25. Pub. 525 sends a refund-only filer to the State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet unless the filer is a nonresident alien or one of its numbered statements is true (other year, non-income-tax refund, 0% rate, refund above the sales-tax difference, last estimated payment in 2025, AMT, unused credits, dependent, joint state return); negative 2024 taxable income is not among them, and the i1040gi p. 89 worksheet (refund.line1 to line9) has no negative-income step. The encoding follows that route; when other itemized deductions were also recovered, rec (Worksheet 2) applies the reduction (rec.negative_ti, rec.line11_negative). The 'You had taxable income' quote is a condition of Pub. 525's general full-inclusion rule, not of the worksheet route.

unruled:s2#1.2.evidence: i6251 p. 4, line 2h, section 1202 exclusion; i6251 p. 8, charitable contribution of section 170(e) property with a different AMT basis. Section 1202: a sale with the exclusion is refused per sale by sales.special ('small business stock on which you exclude part of the gain (section 1202)'; remedy 'Sales of collectibles, section 1202 stock ... are unsupported'), and box 2c of Form 1099-DIV by div.section1202 ('Form 8949 code Q / Form 6251'). The xrel ruling's citation of sd.small_business_stock is stale: that question is now the section 1244/1242 ordinary loss. Section 170(e): the AMT basis of property the tool can hold is never below its regular basis (AMT depreciation is slower or equal, and stock from an ISO exercise has the higher AMT basis), so a basis-limited gift gives an AMT deduction at least as large and the line 2r adjustment can only lower AMTI; the bound on line 4 stays an upper bound. Gifts of business property are also a disposition refused by the asset screen; vehicles, pass-through interests, inventory and intellectual property are refused by gift.special.

unruled:s2#1.3.evidence: i6251 pp. 3, 7-8, depletion, long-term contracts, research and experimental costs, pollution control amortization, AMT Form 8990. Each is refused on Schedule C by sc.screened: depletion and Form 8990 by sc.special ('it mines, drills or cuts timber and deducts depletion', 'its interest deduction is limited by Form 8990', 'you chose to spread research costs over several years', 'it has a license or other cost that must be written off over several years'); long-term contracts by sc.method_other ('long-term contracts'); research costs deducted currently need no adjustment when the filer materially participated (i6251 line 2r caution, 'Don't make this adjustment for costs paid or incurred in connection with an activity in which you materially participated'), and sc.passive false (no material participation) refuses through sc.screened. Section 169 pollution control amortization is an amortization election the asset and Schedule C lines do not offer. Rental and royalty depletion are refused by rental.depletion and royalty.depletion.

unruled:s2#1.4.evidence: i6251 p. 1, Who Must File, statements 2 and 3, and the Form 8801 reference. The credits that trigger them are refused: a general business credit by s3.business_credit_any; the personal-use Form 8911 credit by s3.ev_equipment; Form 8834 by s3.other_credit; the prior-year minimum tax credit by s3.prior_amt_if_forms (2024 AMT with an item on 2024 Form 6251 line 2e, 2f, 2i to 2t or 3, 'If you are not sure, answer Yes; a Yes ends the interview here') and s3.prior_forms_if_forms ('Is any of those forms Form 3800, 8396, 8801, ...', which covers a Form 8801 carryforward). 2024 AMT from exclusion items only gives no 2025 credit. So a return that reaches s2.amt claims none of them and Form 6251 is not required by statements 2 and 3.

unruled:scope#1.2.evidence: i1040gi pp. 34, 36. Form 4972: retirement.special includes retirement.lump_sum_if_born_before_averaging_date (the lump-sum distribution question) and refuses. Form 2555: sa.excluded_income refuses f1040.line16 (executed, refusal at sa.excluded_income), so the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet case never computes.

unruled:f4137#1.1.evidence: f4137 p. 2, Line 1, Columns (c) and (d), 'include any allocated tips ... shown on your Form(s) W-2, box 8, unless you can prove that your unreported tips are less'. Allocated tips are refused: s2.w2_marks (asked of every filer with a W-2, 'Does any have an amount in box 8 ...'; help 'Box 8 is tips the employer assigned to you ... A Yes ends the interview here') makes s2.other true, which refuses. Report timing is covered: f4137row.col_c help 'Tips reported in January 2026 for December 2025 count in 2026, not here'; f4137row.col_d help 'Count tips reported late for 2025 too'. December 2024 tips reported timely in January 2025 fall out of both columns (c) and (d) under the questions' wording, so lines 2 and 3 are both lower and line 4 and the tax are unchanged (presentation only).

unruled:f4137#1.2.evidence: f4137 p. 2, Columns (c) and (d), timely and late reporting. f4137row.col_d help 'Count tips reported late for 2025 too' (late tips belong to the year earned); f4137row.col_c help 'Tips reported in January 2026 for December 2025 count in 2026, not here' (timely January report moves the tips to 2026). The remaining case, December 2024 tips reported timely in January 2025, drops out of both columns (c) and (d) together, so line 4 (c minus d), line 6 and the tax do not change.

unruled:f4137#1.3.evidence: f4137 p. 2, 'the $20 rule applies separately to the tips you received while working for each employer'. person.f4137_under20 asks for tips not reported 'because the tips at one job came to less than $20 in a calendar month', and its interview help says 'in a month in which the cash and card tips at that job came to $20 or more'; the test is per employer as the source says.

unruled:f4137#1.4.evidence: f4137 p. 1, 'If you believe you're an employee and you received Form 1099-MISC ... don't use this form'. Form 4137 takes only tips per employer (f4137row.col_c/col_d, reached through scope.tips_unreported 'Tips not reported in full to an employer'); no question puts Form 1099 pay there. Pay from a firm that treated the filer as a contractor is asked by scope.contractor_pay ('did a firm pay you ... as an independent contractor, when you believe you were its employee, without taking out social security or Medicare tax?') and goes to Form 8919 (f8919firm.wages, help 'With a Form 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC, this is usually its amount').

unruled:f4137row#1.1.evidence: f4137 p. 2, Columns (c) and (d), allocated tips in W-2 box 8; RRTA. Box 8 is refused through s2.w2_marks ('an amount in box 8 ... A Yes ends the interview here'), which makes s2.other refuse. RRTA work is refused on f4137.line8 when person.rrta ('Don't use Form 4137 to report tips received for work covered by the Railroad Retirement Tax Act').

unruled:f4137row#1.2.evidence: f4137 p. 2, Columns (c) and (d), timely and late reporting, 10th-day rule. As f4137#1.2: col_c help moves December 2025 tips reported in January 2026 to 2026, col_d help counts late-reported 2025 tips; the residual December 2024 case moves columns (c) and (d) together and changes no tax. The 10th-day weekend rule is the definition of timely and changes no amount the filer enters beyond that help.

unruled:f4137row#1.3.evidence: f4137 p. 2, Line 1, columns (a) and (b) and the over-five-employers statement. The collection note says 'columns (a) and (b) name the employer and change no amount'; the employer rows are a collection with no limit of five, and lines 2 and 3 total all rows, which is what the attachment rule produces. Names, EINs and the attachment are paper presentation.

unruled:f8919#1.1.evidence: f8919 p. 1, Who must file. scope.contractor_pay asks the three conditions together: 'did a firm pay you ... as an independent contractor, when you believe you were its employee, without taking out social security or Medicare tax?'; the firms are then listed in f8919firm, each with f8919firm.reason (codes A, C, G, H). The reason help says 'If none of these fits but you believe you were an employee, choose the third and send Form SS-8 to the IRS by the day you file. With the last one, do not send Form SS-8.' So eligibility, the code and the SS-8 rule are asked.

unruled:f8919#1.2.evidence: f8919 p. 2, Line 6, 'Also enter this amount on Form 8959, line 3'. The claim is false: f8959.line3 sums person.f8919_wages over persons ('Wages from Form 8919, line 6'), so line 6 reaches the Additional Medicare Tax. The per-firm columns (a), (b), (d) and (e) are presentation: the f8919firm note says they 'identify the firm and the IRS letter and change no amount'; one code per row is enforced by the single-choice f8919firm.reason.

unruled:f8919firm#1.1.evidence: f8919 p. 1, columns (a), (b), (d), (e). The f8919firm note: 'columns (a), (b), (d) and (e) identify the firm and the IRS letter and change no amount'. The SS-8 point is false: f8919firm.reason help says 'With the last one [code H], do not send Form SS-8.'

unruled:f8919firm#1.2.evidence: f8919 p. 1, 'If married, complete a separate Form 8919 for each spouse'. f8919firm is a collection within person ('For this person (you, or your spouse on a joint return) — Which firms paid you in that way in 2025?'), and f8919 is one per person (note: 'Lines 6 to 13 of one person's Form 8919, from that person's firms'); lines 7 to 10 use that person's own wages, so the wage base is applied per spouse.

unruled:oi8z#1.1.evidence: p525 p. 32, Court awards and damages: the medical-care exception for non-physical emotional distress, the pre-September 13, 1995 agreements, and attorney fees included in income. For kind taxable_damages, oi8z.injury asks only about a physical injury or sickness (Yes refuses); with No, oi8z.amount asks 'How much of it is income for 2025?' with no help on these rules, so the medical-care part may be taxed and an award net of a contingent fee may be understated. Low.

unruled:oi8z#1.2.evidence: p525 pp. 32-34: credit card insurance benefits net of premiums, a free tour at FMV, sale of an expected inheritance. None is one of the five prepared kinds of oi8z.kind (RTAA, kickbacks, fiduciary fees, found property, taxable damages); each is 'Something else' (other), and oi8z.figured is true for kind other, which refuses ('Line 8z items other than RTAA payments and kickbacks are outside this tool'); oi8z.kind help says choosing any other kind ends the interview.

unruled:sa#1.3.evidence: i1040sca p. 8, reduce line 8a by Form 8396 line 3. s3.mcc ('Were you ... issued a mortgage credit certificate (MCC) ... for the loan on your main home?') is asked when line 8a is above zero (s3.mcc_if_interest), and a Yes refuses on s3.line7: 'A mortgage credit certificate gives the mortgage interest credit (Form 8396), which also reduces the home mortgage interest deducted on Schedule A; this tool does not prepare it.'

unruled:sa#1.4.evidence: i1040sca p. 10, Amounts You Can't Deduct, 'Gifts to foreign organizations'. The sa.line11 prompt and help leave out political gifts, raffle tickets, tuition, club dues, gifts to people, repaid amounts and the state-credit part, and sa.gifts help defines charities, but nothing leaves out a gift made directly to a foreign charity; it is deducted. Medium.

unruled:sa#1.5.evidence: i1040sca p. 12, claim of right over $3,000. s3.repaid_income ('In 2025, did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay back more than $3,000 that you had reported as income in an earlier year?') is asked in the rare-credits group, and a Yes refuses on s3.line14: 'Repayment of income of an earlier year (Schedule 3 line 13b or Schedule A line 16) ... which this tool does not figure.' The claim missed this question because it is on Schedule 3.

unruled:tipjob#1.1.evidence: i1040gi p. 103, option 2, the Form 4070 total. tipjob.tips interview help: 'You may instead take the total of the tips you reported to this employer on Form 4070 or a similar monthly report, which can be more accurate if box 1 or box 5 of the W-2 is over $176,100.'

unruled:clcw_next_year#1.1.evidence: i1040sd p. 10, 'If you excluded canceled debt from income in 2025, see Pub. 4681.' Canceled debt excluded from income is a Yes to s1.cod_unsupported ('it was canceled in a bankruptcy case or while you ... were insolvent, or is otherwise excluded from income (Form 982 ...)'), asked under s1.cod_any of every filer, which refuses s1.cod_refused. No attribute reduction of the carryovers arises on a return the tool prepares. As the earlier clcw#1.1 ruling, rechecked.

unruled:clcw_next_year#1.2.evidence: p550 p. 103; i1040sd p. 10, 'can be deducted only on the return of the spouse who actually had the loss.' The 2025 side is refused: clcw.spouse_screen asks whether 'the 2024 return these figures come from was a joint return, and for 2025 you are not filing a joint return with the same spouse' and refuses clcw.line1. Separate returns are now prepared (s3.mfs is gone), and this screen, not s3.mfs, is what refuses a 2025 separate return after a 2024 joint one. The carryover figured here (clcw_next_year) is the 2025 return's own carryover; dividing it if the spouses file separately in 2026 is a 2026 return's question and changes no 2025 amount.

unruled:f1116#1.1.evidence: i1116 p. 2, 'Generally, if you take the credit for any eligible foreign taxes, you can't take any part of that year's foreign taxes as a deduction'; p514 p. 38. sa.foreign_tax_deduct ('Do you want to deduct the foreign taxes you ... paid instead of taking a credit for them?', help 'This tool does not figure the deduction; to go on without it, answer No') is asked of every filer with foreign tax (sa.foreign_tax_deduct_if_tax on ftc.has_tax); a Yes sets sa.unsupported, which refuses Schedule A and the return (eval /tmp/xrr/rinv/deduct.json, f1116.c1_unlimited with the Yes: ftc.credit, s3.line1 refused at sa.unsupported). On a No, Schedule A line 6 (other taxes, where a foreign income tax would be deducted) is a constant zero (sa.line6 copies sa.zero) and f1116.line3a_itemized reads only lines 4 and 5e, so a return that takes the credit never deducts any of the year's foreign tax.

unruled:f1116#1.2.evidence: i1116 p. 18, 'If you report on the cash basis, you can choose to take the credit for accrued taxes by checking the “Accrued” box'. Form 1116 is prepared only for tax withheld at source and reported in U.S. dollars on Form 1099-DIV box 7, 1099-INT box 6 or a similar statement (f1116col.tax_div, f1116col.tax_int; ftc.statements, help 'Answer No if you paid any of the tax to another country yourself'). Tax withheld at source accrues and is paid when it is withheld, so line 8 is the same on either basis. Tax paid directly to a foreign country, where the year of accrual and the year of payment can differ, is a No to ftc.statements and refuses at f1116.not_on_statement (eval /tmp/xrr/rinv/nostmt.json: ftc.credit and s3.line1 refused there). The Paid/Accrued box is filing presentation and changes no amount.

unruled:f1116#1.3.evidence: i1116 p. 2, 'Don't use Form 1116 to figure a credit for taxes paid to the U.S. Virgin Islands. Instead, use Form 8689'. s3.virgin_islands ('Does part of your 2025 tax belong to the U.S. Virgin Islands (Form 8689)?', help 'Yes if you ... had income from the U.S. Virgin Islands in 2025 and were not a resident there') is asked of every filer who answers Yes to s3.foreign_any ('ever paid income tax to another country, had income from a U.S. territory ...'), and a Yes refuses the return at s3.line14 (eval /tmp/xrr/rinv/usvi.json: f1040.line24 and line37 refused at s3.virgin_islands_if_foreign). A bona fide U.S. Virgin Islands resident files with the Virgin Islands, not this return.

unruled:f1116#1.4.evidence: cfr-26-1-904-4 p. 4, (c)(3), 'All passive income received during the taxable year that is subject to no withholding tax but is subject to a foreign tax other than a withholding tax shall be treated as one item of income.' The columns hold only tax withheld at source (f1116col.tax_div 'Foreign tax withheld at source on the dividends ... Form 1099-DIV box 7', f1116col.tax_int box 6). A foreign tax that is not a withholding tax is paid by the filer to the foreign country, not reported on a payee statement: a No to ftc.statements refuses at f1116.not_on_statement (eval /tmp/xrr/rinv/nostmt.json), a tax entered in ftc.taxes but not in a column refuses at f1116.tax_mismatch, and foreign taxes from a Schedule K-1 refuse in k1p (box 21) and k1s (box 16 code F). No prepared return holds passive income taxed only by a non-withholding tax. A fund's box 7 tax is classed as withholding tax, the reading of amb.2025.f1116_high_taxed.

unruled:f1116#1.5.evidence: i1116 p. 17, 'Attach a statement listing the separate expenses included on lines 3a and 3b.' f1116.line3a (Schedule A lines 4 and 5e, or the standard deduction f1040.line12e) and f1116.line3b (Schedule 1 line 26 less line 21) are computed from amounts on the return; the attached list is filing information and changes no amount.

unruled:f1116col#1.1.evidence: i1116 pp. 9-10. The claim that nothing reads the worksheet is wrong: f1116.must_adjust tests qdcg.line5 above zero and qdcg.line23 below qdcg.line24 (or Schedule D Tax Worksheet lines 18, 45 and 46); f1116.exception applies f1116.exception_ceiling ($197,300 single, head of household and married filing separately, $394,600 joint; eval /tmp/xrr/rinv/mfs.json shows 19730000 for mfs) and the $20,000 test on all foreign dividends of the columns (amb.2025.f1116_exception, which can only refuse more); a return that must adjust and has no exception refuses at f1116.adjust (fixtures f1116.c6_adjust_ceiling and c7_adjust_20000, evaluated: refused at f1116.adjust). Line 1a is unadjusted only when no adjustment is required or the exception is taken. Foreign capital gain distributions refuse at f1116.foreign_gain; the AMT refuses at s2.amt (Form 6251); counting Form 4952 line 4g dividends in f1116.div_total can only fail the $20,000 test and refuse.

unruled:f1116col#1.2.evidence: i1116 pp. 17-18. Line 4b: f1116.asset_method refuses when gross foreign income is over $5,000 (f1116.foreign_over) and there is student loan interest (s1.line21), Schedule 1-A car loan interest (s1a.line30) or itemized investment interest (sa.line9) (fixture f1116.c4_asset_method, evaluated: refused at f1116.asset_method); at $5,000 or less all interest may go to U.S. income (i1116 p. 18). Line 2: f1116.itemized_unread refuses an itemizer with state or local income tax on Schedule A line 5a (fixture f1116.c4_state_income_tax, evaluated: refused there); a non-itemizer has none to enter. Line 5: the columns hold only dividends and interest (non-negative), and foreign capital losses refuse at f1116.foreign_gain. Lines 2, 4b and 5 are zero only on returns that pass these refusals.

unruled:f1116col#1.3.evidence: i1116 p. 17, Lines 3a and 3b. Line 3c is defined on the form, not the column: f1116.line3c adds f1116.line3a and f1116.line3b; f1116.line3a is the standard deduction (f1040.line12e, sa.deduction, which holds no Schedule 1-A amount) for a non-itemizer and Schedule A lines 4 and 5e for an itemizer; f1116.line3b is Schedule 1 line 26 (Part II adjustments) less line 21 (student loan interest, interest expense for line 4b) (amb.2025.f1116_3b_items). The Schedule 1-A line 37 senior deduction is on Form 1040 line 13b and enters neither. f1116col.line3g_figured prorates f1116.line3c by f1116col.line3d over f1116.line3e.

unruled:f1116sb#1.1.evidence: i1116 p. 19, Line 10; p514 p. 38, 'you must reduce the amount of any carryback or carryforward by the amount that you would have used had you chosen to claim a credit rather than a deduction in that year.' f1116sbyr.amount takes line 8 of the 2024 Schedule B; f1116sb.prior_year is asked only when a 2025 carryover is generated (f1116sb.prior_year_if_excess); f1116sb.changed names carrybacks, redeterminations and audits. A carryover through a 2024 deduction or election year is neither reduced nor refused.

unruled:f1116sb#1.2.evidence: p514 p. 39. f1116sb.split asks 'Is any of the foreign tax carried into 2025 from a joint return of an earlier year, when this return is not a joint return with the same spouse?' and refuses through f1116sb.split_if_carry. Case (a), a separate 2025 return with tax carried through a joint year: the year before 2025 that held it was a joint return when the joint year is 2024 (a Yes, refused); when a separate year came after the joint year, the allocation was made on that separate return's Schedule B, whose line 8 is what f1116sbyr.amount takes. Case (b), joint origin and joint 2025 through separate years: each spouse's 2024 separate Schedule B already holds the allocated amounts, and f1116sbyr.amount's help says 'On a joint return, add your spouse's amount for the same year', which is the combining rule the claim says is missing.

unruled:f1116sb#1.3.evidence: p514 p. 38, reduction of carryovers 'to or from the tax year of the debt cancellation' for debt excluded in bankruptcy or insolvency. A 2025 exclusion is a Yes to s1.cod_unsupported ('canceled in a bankruptcy case or while you ... were insolvent, or is otherwise excluded from income (Form 982 ...)'), which refuses. A reduction made for a 2024 cancellation is made on the 2024 return's Form 982 and reflected in its carryovers.

unruled:f1116sbyr#1.1.evidence: i1116sb p. 1, Line 2. f1116sb.changed ('Since you filed your 2024 return, has anything changed the foreign tax carried from it, such as a carryback that differs from its estimate, a change in foreign tax for an earlier year, or an audit?') is asked whenever a carryover is claimed (f1116sb.changed_if_carry) and refuses f1116.line35 ('an adjustment on line 2 of Schedule B (Form 1116), which this tool does not figure'). Line 2 is empty only on returns without an adjustment. A carryback with no estimate and a correction of the 2024 line 8 are not named: BUG-0834 (2).

unruled:f8960#1.2.evidence: i8960 p. 7, 'If you're making the section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election ... check the corresponding checkbox'; p. 4, without the NIIT election the citizen spouse figures NII and MAGI alone with the $125,000 threshold. f8960 has no election item or question; scope.nonresident ('neither a U.S. citizen nor a U.S. resident for tax') can be answered No for a spouse treated as a resident under a section 6013(g) election, and the tool then figures the NIIT on combined amounts with $250,000. A section 6013(h) couple (a spouse nonresident for part of 2025) answers Yes and is refused.

unruled:gift#1.3.evidence: i8283 pp. 1-2; cfr-26-1-170a-13 p. 3. Whether Form 8283 is filed above $500, the Section A entries (donee, description, dates, basis, method) and the e-file data are filing information the filer keeps (the form's note: 'Dates, descriptions and donee details remain in underlying records'); the deduction amount is asked, and the $5,000 Section B case is refused (gift.section_b, gift.special). As the earlier gift#1.2 ruling.

unruled:qdcg#1.1.evidence: i1040gi p. 38, line 2 footnote (Form 2555). sa.excluded_income ('did you ... live or work abroad, in Puerto Rico or in American Samoa, and leave the income you earned there out of this return?'; help: 'These are the exclusions of Form 2555 ... A Yes ends the interview here') refuses every Form 2555 filer, so the Foreign Earned Income Tax Worksheet never applies.

unruled:qdcg#1.2.evidence: i1040gi p. 38, line 3. The Form 2555 footnote: refused by sa.excluded_income as in qdcg#1.1. The Form 1040 line 7b box ('be sure you checked the box') is a checkbox on the printed return and changes no amount; line 3 takes Form 1040 line 7a.

unruled:sb#1.2.evidence: i1040sb pp. 1-2, line 5 payer list. sb.ordinary_dividends asks the total of box 1a; the payer-by-payer listing on line 5 and the overflow statement are the printed layout and change no amount (line 6 is the total).

unruled:f5329#1.4.evidence: i5329 p. 8. f8889.excess_withdrawn asks 'Did you withdraw from your HSA any excess contributions (yours or your employer's) or the earnings on them, in 2025, or in 2026 by the due date of your 2025 return including extensions, or will you by that date?' and refuses Form 8889 lines 2, 13 and 14b, so a timely withdrawal never reaches line 47. A withdrawal in the 6-month window after a timely filed return is made with an amended return, not this one.

unruled:retirement#1.4.evidence: i1040gi p. 27. The statement explaining a rollover into a qualified plan, or one made in 2026, is an attachment; the amount rolled over within 60 days is asked (retirement.rollover) and excluded from line 4b.

unruled:retirement#1.5.evidence: i5329 p. 5. The statement with the child's or eligible adoptee's name, age and TIN (or the death documentation) is an attachment; exception 19 is accepted (retirement.exception states the 1-year period and eligible adoptee) and capped by person.x_cap19 ($5,000 per birth or adoption).

unruled:sli#1.1.evidence: i1040gi pp. 98-99. sli.unqualified_any's help ('School costs are tuition, fees, room and board, books, supplies and the like, for a degree or certificate program. Someone you could have claimed as a dependent but for that person's income or joint return, or because you could be claimed yourself, counts as your dependent here.') covers category 3 and the degree or certificate program, which the claim missed (it read the prompt alone). Left open: nothing asks whether the school was an eligible educational institution or the student an eligible student, so a loan for such costs is counted as qualified; recorded with the false-no finding of gate:sli.unqualified_any_if_any#1 in BUG-0881. Low.

unruled:ssb#1.1.evidence: i1040gi p. 31. Even when ssb.ira_covered is answered No, ira.cov_gate (social security benefits, traditional IRA contributions, and ira.anyone_covered: anyone covered or, filing separately, considered covered through the spouse) refuses person.ira_ssb_figured and so the worksheet. Evaluated: fixture stage16.ira.i10 with person[taxpayer].ira_work_plan true and ssb.ira_covered false gives f1040.line6b refused at ira.cov_gate. A contributor whose spouse alone is covered is counted by ira.cov_count / ira.mfs_spouse_covered_if_asked in the same gate.

unruled:person#1.1.evidence: i1040sse p. 4; i1040sc p. 14. As the ruling of the same claim earlier in this round (person#1, and person#5 before it): sc.statutory asks whether the Schedule C is statutory employee income or notary public fees and sc.screened refuses the Schedule C, so no such line 31 reaches person.se_line2 (stage14.eic.wsb_only_business, sc[odd].statutory true refuses at sc[odd].screened).

unruled:person#1.2.evidence: i2441 p. 4 and p503 p. 11 (a statutory employee's Schedule C line 1 is earned income). sc.statutory asks whether the Schedule C is statutory employee income or notary public fees, and sc.screened refuses that Schedule C, so no statutory-employee Schedule C reaches person.dc_earned; the same screen as person#1.

unruled:person#1.3.evidence: p560 p. 16, Employer matching contributions: "If you choose a matching contribution less than 3%, the percentage must be at least 1%". person.employer_max allows matching up to 3% of compensation, the plan's maximum; a plan that elected a lower match for 2025 makes any matching above that rate more than the deductible amount, and person.plan_screen asks whether there are "contributions that are more than the maximum deductible amount" and person.plan_screened refuses the person's retirement lines on Yes. The reading relies on the screen's wording reaching a filer who knows the plan's elected rate; no amount is computed for such contributions.

unruled:person#1.4.evidence: p590b p. 28. As the prior ruling on this claim: retirement.exc_amount tells the filer to enter, for exception 22, no more than 50% of the present value of the IRA or plan account; person.x_c22 applies the $10,300 cap. [Restamped unchanged from the ruling of earlier claim #4 under prompt_sha a0dc7c50: same form, same quoted text, same cited page, same item and effect.]

unruled:person#1.5.evidence: p590b p. 28. As the prior ruling on this claim: retirement.exc_amount caps exception 23 at the total interest in the IRA or plan account minus $1,000; retirement.early_screen refuses an emergency distribution within 3 years after an unrepaid earlier one; person.x_two23 refuses more than one in a year. [Restamped unchanged from the ruling of earlier claim #5 under prompt_sha a0dc7c50: same form, same quoted text, same cited page, same item and effect.]

unruled:person#1.6.evidence: i8863 pp. 1, 3. As the earlier person#3 ruling: f8863.ban asks about a post-2015 denial or reduction needing Form 8862 and the 2-year and 10-year bans for the return's American opportunity credit, and f8863.ban_refused refuses line 7 (stage19.example.jack_kay, f8863.ban true refuses f8863.line7, line8 and f1040.line29).

unruled:person#1.7.evidence: i1040gi p. 95 (reservist repayments not deductible); i8606 p. 9, "Include on line 1 any repayment of a qualified reservist distribution". As the earlier person#2 ruling: scope.other_income lists "a repayment to an IRA of a qualified reservist distribution (Form 8606 line 1)" and refuses the return, so no such repayment reaches person.ira_trad.

unruled:f1116col#1.4.evidence: cfr-26-1-904-4 p. 4, (c)(3), 'passive income is not treated as subject to a withholding tax ... when a credit is disallowed in full for such foreign tax, for example, under section 901(k)'. ftc.taxes asks the creditable tax 'leaving out tax withheld on a dividend from stock held fewer than 16 days', while the column asks the box 7 amount 'as reported'; when a section 901(k) tax is left out the two differ and f1116.tax_mismatch refuses line 35 (eval /tmp/xrr/rinv/k901.json: ftc.taxes $500, column $600, refused at f1116.tax_mismatch). Income bearing only a non-withholding foreign tax is not on a prepared return (see f1116#1.4: f1116.not_on_statement).

unruled:f1116col#1.5.evidence: i1116 p. 11; cfr-26-1-904-4 p. 4. The claim that no item allocates deductions or tests the groups is wrong: f1116.exp_hi and f1116.exp_lo apportion line 3c and the home mortgage interest to the 15-percent-or-more and under-15-percent groups by gross income over line 3e, f1116.net_hi/net_lo take the net income, f1116.limit_hi/limit_lo apply 37 percent (f1116.high_tax_rate), and f1116.high_taxed refuses line 35 when either group's tax exceeds its limit (fixture f1116.c3_htko_over, evaluated: refused at f1116.high_taxed), so no HTKO column is needed on a prepared return. The test uses unadjusted gross income, before the 904(b) adjustments. With ratable apportionment a group's deductions exceed its income only when all groups are at zero, so the (c)(2)(ii) reallocation moves nothing (amb.2025.f1116_high_taxed).

unruled:f1040#1.8.evidence: i1040gi p. 39, Line 26, 'If you and your spouse paid joint estimated tax but are now filing separate income tax returns, you can divide the amount paid in any way you choose as long as you both agree. If you can't agree, you must divide the payments in proportion to each spouse's individual tax'. Unchanged since the xrel ruling: f1040.line26 is a supplied total; its question ('How much estimated tax did you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) pay for 2025 in all, counting any 2024 refund applied to 2025?') and help ('On a joint return add what each of you paid, even if you paid separately') address only a joint return. Separate returns are supported, so a separate filer with joint payments is not told to enter only a share (BUG-0894, open).

unruled:f1040#1.9.evidence: i8863 p. 1, Form 8862 may be required; i8863 p. 3, 2- and 10-year bans. The claim missed f8863.ban ('Has the IRS ever denied or reduced an American opportunity credit you claimed, for more than a math error, or ...', help 'A Yes is outside what this tool prepares and ends the interview here'), asked when an American opportunity credit is claimed (f8863.ban_refused, which refuses f8863.line7). Executed on a copy of f8863.json stage19.example.jack_kay: line 29 $1,000 with f8863.ban false; with f8863.ban true, f1040.line29 and line 24 are refusals at f8863.ban_refused.

unruled:s2#1.5.evidence: i6251 p. 13, Form 2555 filers with an AMT capital gain excess complete Part III with modifications. sa.excluded_income (Form 2555, Form 4563, Puerto Rico) refuses the return; executed on a copy of scope.ch11.wage_only_debtor (chapter 11 No) with sa.excluded_income true: f1040.line16 and line 24 are refusals at sa.excluded_income. Lines 13-15 never run for a Form 2555 filer.

unruled:s2#1.6.evidence: i1040gi p. 112; i1040sse p. 2, Form 4029, totalization agreement (EAS), notary fees (EN), foreign government employment, Form 2555, chapter 11. person.se_screen ('an approved exemption from self-employment tax on religious grounds (Form 4361 or Form 4029) ... or earnings exempt under a social security agreement with another country or from work for a foreign government', 'A Yes is outside what this tool prepares') refuses through person.se_screened; notary fees by the Schedule C statutory-employee screen (tick 'Its income is from a statutory employee W-2 job, or notary fees', 'Answer Yes also if only part of its income is notary fees'), sc.screened; Form 2555 by sa.excluded_income (executed: line 16 and line 24 refused); a chapter 11 debtor by scope.chapter11 through scope.other_income.

unruled:rental#1.11.evidence: p527 p. 28 (quoted, checked). rental.ws51 (home use in 2025 and not excluded) is the only Worksheet 5-1 refusal; rental.prior_any asks about a loss 'held back (not deducted) on your 2024 return or an earlier one' with help 'Look for Form 8582 in your 2024 return', which points away from a Worksheet 5-1 carryover. A carryover into a year without home use is neither asked nor refused. Same as BUG-0778 (open, low).

unruled:f2441#1.3.evidence: i2441 p. 3, Column (b), quoted; p503 p. 3. A qualifying person must be the filer's dependent (dependent.dc_qp requires dependent.claimed; a non-dependent qualifying person is refused at f2441.nondependent_gate). dependent.tin asks for an 'SSN, ITIN or ATIN issued on or before the due date ... or have you applied for an ITIN or ATIN', and dependent.claimed refuses through dependent.claimed_no_tin ('Each dependent must be listed with an SSN (or ITIN or ATIN) ... A dependent child who was born and died in 2025 without an SSN, entered as "Died" ... is outside this tool'). The column (c) box is encoded: dependent.dc_line2c from dependent.dc_over12_care and dependent.dc_incapable. dependent.dc_count's cite records the TIN route.

unruled:f2441#1.4.evidence: i2441 p. 3, Column (c), quoted. dcprov.tin_kind (printed 1(c)) is an enum with tin, tax_exempt ('enter "Tax-Exempt"'), lafcp ('enter "LAFCP"'), see_statement and employer; the interview offers the same five answers. The 'none' entry on line 1 column (a) for a filer completing only Part III is a name column, which the dcprov note says is written by the filer and not modelled; presentation only, no amount.

unruled:f8853c#1.1.evidence: i8853 p. 8, Policyholder, 'The policyholder is required to report the income, even if payment is assigned to a third party or parties'. f8853c.line17 follows the form's own instruction, box 1 of the Forms 1099-LTC with Per diem checked, and its interview prompt ('How much long-term care insurance was paid at a set rate? Add box 1 of those forms.') does not limit it to payments to the filer. But the entry question s1.ltc_payout asks 'were you ... paid by a long-term care insurance policy', and nothing tells a policyholder whose benefits went straight to the care provider that they count; such a filer can answer No and Section C is not reached. Low: line 26 changes only where the per diem exceeds both $420 a day and the costs less reimbursements.

unruled:f8853c#1.2.evidence: i8853 p. 9, Line 22, 'services required to treat a chronically ill individual under a plan of care prescribed by a licensed health care practitioner'; p. 8, Chronically Ill Individual, 'certified within the past 12 months'. The certification itself is carried by the payments: a qualified contract pays only for a chronically ill insured (p. 8, 'including the requirement that the insured must be a chronically ill individual'), nonqualified contracts are refused (f8853c.nonqualified), and line 22 counts costs only 'during those days' the payments were for. What is dropped is 'required to treat a chronically ill individual' in the f8853c.line22 source, recorded in BUG-0916 (low). The interview prompt ('What did this person's long-term care cost during those days?', help 'such as nursing home or home care bills') omits it too; BUG-0916's proposed fix names only the form source, so the lead should extend it to the interview prompt. Line 22 matters only where it exceeds $420 a day.

unruled:dependent#1.3.evidence: i1040gi p. 17, "If you have more than four dependents, check the box under Dependents on page 1 of Form 1040 or 1040-SR and include a statement". The tool lists every dependent (the dependent collection) and computes the same amounts for five dependents as for four; the checkbox and the continuation statement are how the paper form shows rows that do not fit. No amount or eligibility changes; checked: no line in f1040.yaml or dependent.yaml produces the box, which is a printed-form layout matter. Re-ruled on the new sample (2026-11-16): the claim adds the row (5) and row (6) boxes (lived with you, in the United States, full-time student, disabled), which are also printed-form entries; the tests they report are computed (dependent.eic_child, dependent.claimed) and change no amount.
